Great location. Yes it's a huge hotel as it's used for conventions but that didn't stop it from being a great place.

My recent night at Conrad Chicago felt perfectly calibrated rather than rushed; I lingered over breakfast without feeling guilty about my short stay duration. The ambiance strikes an ideal balance where quiet reigns supreme despite being centrally located near bustling streets that occasionally hum gently in the background, creating a soothing urban lullaby. Sleep was profound and uninterrupted thanks to premium linens and blackout curtains that truly deliver on luxury promises.

I never write these reviews, but felt that it was important to state that this hotel should not be the #1 2008 travelers choice. Terrible Service, Lazy Doormen/bellmen/concierge/valet, Lack of Respect, allow dogs to bark all morning after multiple complaints, Phantom charges to room, front dest at checkout and checkin were pompus. The icing on the cake was me watching the doormen stand and watch while a father tried to open a door to push his stroller through with his infant son, and the doorman watched on doing nothing. Me and my girlfriend are young, look young in how we dress, but in all honesty make more money than most...and we were treated like cheap poor kids. I had dinner reservations at Spaiggia and wanted to order a car to pick us up, the concierge exclaimed that, 'You know its not jeans and running shoes right Mr. Blank?' Assuming I was too dumb to realize that a 5 star $200/person restraunt wont allow tennis shoes because I am young? Very Dissapointed. Very nice looking, comfortable beds, great room service, contemporary, younger crowd, but service was terrible.

The four nights here stretched far too long given the stale air, chipped vanity mirror, and bathroom that felt like an afterthought--shower pressure weaker than a drizzle--while my overpriced, unrefurbished room overlooked nothing but a concrete plaza, not even worth the premium. Breakfast was just sad pastries; no surprise.

Stayed at James Hotel last weekend for a short but sweet city escape, and honestly? This place elevated my whole trip--beyond just being a nice hotel. From the moment I checked in with the super-friendly host at reception (she knew the area's best spots offbeat), I was hooked.

The rooms--oh, those sofas! Comfy enough to nap in, but with crisp linens and that neutral palette? Pure rest mode. And the bathtub?! Perfectly deep for my legs to stretch out after hours of exploring. My breakfast (on the house) hit the spot too: avocado toast with local honey, black coffee so rich it deserved its own praise. The service is effortless yet thoughtful--they remembered I preferred tea without sugar and had my mug ready when I asked.

The location's unbeatable--steps from that little bakery with the warm cinnamon buns, and a breeze walk to the waterfront. No need for taxis here.

Check-in was sluggish given how short our scheduled stay felt like an afterthought rather than a planned escape. The room itself offered nothing but darkness despite claiming to face downtown; peering out revealed only towering brick walls blocking any potential city lights, leaving us feeling isolated from the vibrant energy outside. Noise became my constant companion throughout the night as neighbors argued loudly just inches behind thin plaster partitions while an elevator dinged and clattered incessantly above our heads. I managed barely two hours of sleep before tossing again at 4 AM due to the relentless hum of ventilation systems mixing with distant sirens. The bed felt stiff and uncomfortable, failing to cradle my weary body after a long flight where legroom was nonexistent anyway. Breakfast options were limited toast varieties that tasted reheated rather than fresh off an oven.

Check-in was a nightmare from the start; the lobby felt more like an office than a welcoming hotel space and we waited nearly twenty minutes just for someone to notice us at the desk. The front desk agent seemed incredibly distracted by her phone while our luggage sat ignored on a random bench until another guest had to intervene. Our room, supposedly a garden view suite, was actually facing a construction site with constant banging sounds that never stopped despite requesting an early change multiple times over two days of our stay. The bed felt completely unsupportive and the mattress creaked loudly every time we shifted weight during intimacy or sleep trying to get comfortable.

Honestly, I left this Homewood feeling really let down. The room itself was adequate, I guess, but nothing about it felt refreshed or well-maintained. Specifically, the bathroom grout looked genuinely stained, which is a surprisingly jarring thing to notice when you're trying to unwind after travel. And don't even get me started on the Wi-Fi; it kept dropping out at random intervals, making it impossible to properly work from my laptop half the time I was here. It's clear that some upkeep needs serious attention across different areas of the property. For what you pay, I expected a much higher level of consistency and cleanliness--it felt more like a temporary stopgap than a place designed for comfort. I won't be recommending this one to friends looking for a reliable stay.

We just arrived from a 3 nights stay at the Sofitel Chicago Water Tower. It was faboulous. Fine Linen, nice room with bigs windows, bathroom with a shower, flat TV. Check for the deals on the Sofitel website, we had 3 nights for the price of two !

Just wrapped up a fantastic stay at the InterContinental; honestly, it exceeded my expectations from start to finish. From the moment we arrived, the service was impeccable--the concierge team was incredibly proactive without ever being intrusive. Our room itself was stunning, boasting such a lovely view of the city skyline that we spent half our mornings just sipping coffee and admiring it. The bedding was luxurious, making for some seriously restful nights after long days of sightseeing. We ate at one of the restaurants last night, and I have to rave about the seafood platter; truly gourmet quality! While the entire property is beautiful, the rooftop bar offered a perfect blend of chic ambiance and fantastic cocktails. If you're looking for a stay where comfort, service, and location all align perfectly, this is absolutely it. We are already planning our return trip!

Just back from a business trip. The Homewood is in a great location just off the Magnificent Mile, includes a great breakfast, heavy hors d'ouevres for dinner with beer and all for a pre-paid rate of $129. Without a doubt the best value in Chicago for a long, long time.

Honestly, the Knickerbocker was just underwhelming; far too overpriced for what I experienced--the room felt dated and breakfast was disappointingly lackluster, making for a really tough stay overall.

The Sheraton hotel's cramped bathroom with low water pressure was a frustrating start to my stay. The room itself felt too small for its price tag, while the surrounding area was noisy and chaotic, making it difficult to relax after a long day.

Just had an amazing stay at Hotel Allegro downtown and honestly couldn't stop smiling throughout my entire trip here. The lobby area feels so welcoming with those warm brass accents catching the sunlight streaming through the huge windows right when you walk in after a long flight, which immediately lifted my mood completely before even checking into my room on the fourth floor where everything was spotless despite being older than most other places I've stayed lately because they clearly take pride in maintaining character without letting things get dusty or neglected at all.

We stayed here as an alternative spot for a friend's wedding. The price was about 50% to 65% of what it costs to stay at similar hotels in the area. First the minuses. 1.) The standard rooms are small. if you want a little more space you might want to upgrade. 2.) Since the hotel has been recently rehabbed you can see some of the stuff that the covered or painted. 3.) There really are no views from the hotel. Now the plusses. 1.) The shower is AWESOME. Probably one of the best hotel showers I've seen. Rain shower with wand, great pressure and the enclosure didn't leak like a lot of these shower stalls do. Very nice. 2.) The fixtures and finishes in the rooms were top notch. Very modern and clean. 3.) The bed was great. Better than some hotels that promote their beds. Great nights sleep. Overall. This is a great space for a trip where you are not going to be spending much time in the room. If you were in town for a conference or for work where you will need to spread out your stuff it might not work. Anyone else should really like the experience. All I care about when I travel is having a nice bed and a good shower to relax in after a long day. If you are the same this is a good spot for you.

I visited Chicago with my two teenage daughters. Homewood Suites is amazing. The complimentary breakfast and receptions offer so much variety. The hotel was within walking distance to many places to eat and shop. We got caught in a thunderstorm, and got soaking wet. I dried all our clothes in the dryer right in the hotel! The Homewood Suites was so much like home. The suite was very spacious and had everything we needed. The hotel had lots of brochures and suggestions for dining and activities. The staff was so friendly and helpful. Chicago is an amazing place and the Homewood Suites is the place to stay. I would definitely stay there again.
